Cleanup un-wedge, Task R3 (D-8001; plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-cleanup-unwedge.md`, spec §5 and D9 to D11).

A repository-wide `git worktree prune` deletes git's record of every gone worktree of the repository at once, and ccd's cleanup reads those records, so one session's prune holds the cleanup of every lane on a box. This makes the session hook refuse it on every session, and the approval classifier mark it forbidden. A dry run passes. The advice that named the prune now names the scoped removal of one record.

## What changes

- **`ccd/session-hook.sh`.** `APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN_JQ`'s `fmatch` gains a `prune` row (`GITPRE`, `GOPT`, `GITWT`, `GDRY`), and `norm` moves above `fmatch` so the row reads the command as bash runs it. All three modes answer the row: `deny` (a child), `account` (every other session) and `class` (the classifier). Both prefilters gain `*prune*`, so a payload naming no `prune` forks no jq for this arm. The reason names `git -C <main> worktree remove <path>` and says a dry run (`-n`) is allowed. A deny already set is never replaced.
- **`server/src/coord/approvalguard.ts`.** `FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS` gains `{ why: 'git worktree prune' }` with the same grammar, so no approval can rule one.
- **`server/src/wsaudit.ts`.** The `child-record-stale` sentence names `git -C <main> worktree remove <path>`.
- **Tests.** `session-hook-prune-deny.test.ts` (new) iterates `fixtures/prune-deny/must-deny.json` and `must-allow.json` on a child and a top-level session, each on the main thread and in a subagent. It also checks that a deny already set keeps its reason, and that `git status` forks no forbidden-program jq. `session-hook-approval-deny.test.ts` holds the hook's class mode equal to the classifier over both lists. `approvalguard.test.ts` adds the classifier cases and a linearity case. `wsaudit.test.ts` pins the advice and measures the scoped removal on the running git.
- **Note.** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-cleanup-unwedge/r3.md`: step 0 on main, the mutants, the residuals and the departures by slug.

## The grammar

The row applies once the raw text names `prune`. It reads the command with quotes and backslashes removed and splits it into simple commands on `;`, `&`, `|` and newlines. A simple command is refused when its program is `git`, bare or path-qualified, then git's global options (`-C`, `-c`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `--no-pager`, `--bare` and their kin), `worktree`, any flags and `prune`. The program may come at its head or after `$(`, `(`, a backtick or `{`, a shell keyword, assignments, or a wrapper such as `sudo`, `env` or `bash -c`. The command passes when `-n` or `--dry-run` is one of its words. Because the program must be in a command position, `grep "git worktree prune" …` and a commit message naming it pass. Both are on the must-allow list.

## Mutants

Each one was applied to a saved copy, run, and restored with its sha checked. Every one went red.

| # | Mutant | Red in |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | drop the `fmatch` row | `session-hook-prune-deny`: every must-deny command is denied, on all four callers |
| 2 | drop the `-n` / `--dry-run` exception | `session-hook-prune-deny`: every must-allow command passes, on all four callers |
| 3 | drop the global-options group | `session-hook-prune-deny`: must-deny; the misses are exactly the `-C`, `-c`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `--no-pager`, `--bare` rows |
| 4 | drop `*prune*` from the top-level prefilter | `session-hook-prune-deny`: denied on a top-level session; the top-level budget control |
| 5 | answer the row in `deny` mode only | `session-hook-prune-deny`: denied on a top-level session; `session-hook-approval-deny`: must-deny class-mode parity |
| 6 | drop the classifier row | `approvalguard`: `git worktree prune is forbidden`, `git -C x worktree prune is forbidden`, the must-deny census, linearity |
| 7 | drop the classifier's dry-run exception | `approvalguard`: `git worktree prune --dry-run is not forbidden`, no must-allow command is matched |
| 8 | main's `child-record-stale` sentence | `wsaudit`: the advice names the scoped removal and never git worktree prune |

## Residuals (spec §5)

This is an accident guard, not a wall. The following run past it:

- `bash -c` or `eval` with an assembled string, a script file, an alias or a function.
- A `$VAR` program (there is no `xmatch` row).
- `git gc`, which prunes records older than `gc.worktreePruneExpire`, three months by default.
- A wrapper with an option value the grammar does not read.
- A top-level payload over 8 KiB that spells `prune` with quotes.
- The operator's own shell.

`pr""une` is not caught by the classifier and the hook's class mode, so the strict grammar escalates it to the operator. The deny and account modes refuse it.

There is one known false deny, in the safe direction. A backticked or `$(…)`-wrapped `git worktree prune` inside a quoted heredoc or a commit message is refused. Write that text to a file and pass the file.

`ccd/ccd`'s advice texts that name the prune are Task R1's (landing order R3 → R1). Until R1 lands, the hook refuses the command that ccd's advice names.

## Measured versions

git 2.53.0, jq 1.8.1, GNU bash 5.3.9 on the build box. `wsaudit.test.ts` measures the scoped removal on CI's git: with two gone linked trees, removing one exits 0 and leaves the other `prunable`.

## Gates (through `ccrc test`, one at a time)

Green:
- `session-hook-prune-deny` (new): 12 tests.
- `session-hook-account-deny`: 139 tests.
- `session-hook-approval-deny`: 327 tests. One timing pin went red once under load, at a deny/class ratio of 4.2 against a limit of 3.5. On the same input, main's program and this one measured ratios of 2.6 to 3.0 each. The file was green alone.
- `session-hook-merge-deny`: 235 tests.
- `session-hook`: 713 tests.
- `approvalguard`, `wsaudit`, `workflow-control-census`, `single-definition/*`, `dtbd`, `anchors`, `citations`.
- `growth-check` with `GROWTH_CHECK=armed`.
- `secret-mask`, run alone.
- `tsc --noEmit` for the server sources and for `test/tsconfig.tests.json`.

`deviation-refs`: the tree-floor row is red on this branch's base (`4b0614ab1`). That base predates the plan that defines D-8001 (#2297, merged after it). The PR's merge with main carries that plan, and the other rows pass.

The local server selection (vitest-related plus every `session-hook*` suite, 346 files, run in chunks on a loaded box) left these red. None of them touches a changed file:
- `approvals-routes`, `asks-sweep` and `collect-lane-route`: green alone.
- `retire-executors-pin` (timeouts under load average 7.7) and `shadow-journal` (a 20 s timeout): red on the base commit too.
- `child-reclaim-paused-at-server` (its NUL-leading `claimedBy` row): red on the base commit too, on this box's Node 24.

CI is the arbiter for all of these.
